providers.name: Iowa DNR Boone County Des Moines River Water Trail and public water-access inventory
providers.extractionMethod: The official Boone County water-trail map identifies North Fraser and South Fraser as the concrete-ramp endpoints of the constructed portage around the Fraser low-head dam. Coordinates come from the matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory features. Each inventory point was independently checked against current Esri World Imagery and coincides with the water-side end of the visible ramp, so it is retained as the water entry rather than projected to a mid-river flowline. North Fraser is visibly on the river even though the current NHD water polygon ends about 103 feet away; that known hydrography offset is preserved below.

providers.name: Iowa DNR North Raccoon River Water Trail and Sac County Grant Park ramp
providers.extractionMethod: The Iowa DNR water-trail guide identifies Grant Park as the take-out and portage for the Grant rock dam, and Sac County's park record independently confirms a hard-surface boat ramp on the North Raccoon River. The matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory point (GlobalID a2d820d0-9ec9-4e4b-8525-9dc9717b1c10) was aligned with current Esri World Imagery; the water entry is the adjacent candidate-centered NHD river edge at the visible water-side end of that ramp, eight feet from the official access anchor. The farther route-centerline projection is intentionally rejected because it lies in mid-channel rather than at the ramp edge.

providers.name: Story County South Skunk River Water Trail and Lekwa Access ramp
providers.extractionMethod: Story County identifies Lekwa Access #242 at 56156 130th Street as a managed South Skunk River Water Trail access, and the official MyCountyParks record independently documents canoeing and kayaking with photographs of the signed access and its ramp reaching the river. The matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory feature (GlobalID a39ce3e3-b29c-4f3b-8334-4f19ff04c40c) describes a concrete launch with six parking stalls and a 33-foot parking-to-access distance. Current Esri World Imagery places that inventory coordinate at the visible water-side ramp edge immediately south of the 130th Street bridge. It is retained as the water entry; the NHD and route-projected alternatives 23 and 50 feet farther east are rejected because they move into the channel.

providers.name: Wisconsin DNR Plum Creek Landing and Crawford County lower Kickapoo access
providers.extractionMethod: The Wisconsin DNR public-access inventory identifies feature 835 as Plum Creek Landing, a state-owned carry-in on the Kickapoo River, and Crawford County independently lists the Plum Creek/Kickapoo Wild Woods Canoe Landing. Wisconsin River Trips documents the exact Plum Creek-to-Highway-60 trip, while Miles Paddled's Plum-Creek-to-Wauzeka report publishes 43.11429, -90.91274 for this put-in and 43.08471, -90.87906 for the distinct Wauzeka take-out. Current Esri World Imagery places the DNR coordinate at the water-side edge of the visible gravel turnaround. Candidate-centered NHD evidence independently places it inside the river polygon and 18 feet from the Kickapoo flowline, so the exact DNR coordinate is retained as the water entry.

providers.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Upper Illinois River Water Trail WOKA access pin
providers.extractionMethod: Decimal degrees decoded from the coordinate-linked WOKA Whitewater Park pin on the official AGFC Upper Illinois River Water Trail page. The published point is retained as the park/access anchor, not treated as the water entry; the official WOKA site map independently identifies a separate take-out ramp at the west end of the whitewater side channel.

providers.name: WOKA Whitewater Park official site map
providers.extractionMethod: The official WOKA site map labels TAKE OUT at the west roundabout and purpose-built ramp after Drop 8. The coordinate was derived by aligning that uniquely shaped roundabout/ramp with current satellite imagery and selecting the water-side end of the ramp. This is explicitly map-derived rather than a published coordinate and must also pass fresh candidate-centered NHD flowline and water-polygon checks.

providers.name: City of Columbus ADM river-access lease Exhibit A
providers.extractionMethod: The City of Columbus lease exhibit outlines the public access corridor from Southeast 9th Street to a unique sand-bank entry beside a wooded parcel. The exhibit is south-up; its rail line, canal, access road, wooded parcel, and braided-bank geometry were aligned to current satellite imagery before selecting the water-side end of the mapped corridor. Nebraska Game and Parks independently identifies this terminal access as lying on the Platte River about one mile downstream from the mouth of the Loup. Fresh candidate-centered NHD queries must verify the Platte River flowline, water polygon, and zero-gap Loup-Platte confluence topology before this map-derived point can be applied.

providers.name: Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission Susquehanna River Water Trail North Branch Section 4
providers.extractionMethod: Access coordinate transcribed from the official PFBC Section 4 river-access table and converted from whole-second DMS to decimal degrees. The table identifies Indian Head Campground as a ramp on river right at river mile 146.

providers.name: Endless Mountains Heritage Region Susquehanna River Water Trail North Branch 2021 Access Table
providers.extractionMethod: Decimal-degree access coordinates transcribed from pages 13-14 of the 2021 North Branch River Access & Services table. The table independently identifies launch type, river side, parking, and river mile. The published point is retained as the access anchor; the workflow derives the water-entry coordinate independently from candidate-centered NHD hydrography. These newer coordinates supersede the displaced whole-second DMS coordinates in the 2008 PFBC map series.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission State Lands
providers.extractionMethod: The coordinate is the representative/label point stored on the official George D. Syas WMA property polygon (PHA-NGPC-0000104 / 228W). It identifies the WMA as a whole; it is not a published launch, parking, or water-entry coordinate and must never be projected or auto-applied as one.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission Public Fishing Streams
providers.extractionMethod: The coordinate is the centroid recorded for the official George Syas WMA public-fishing stream polygon (PFA-0052), which covers a reach of the Loup River. It locates the fishable area, not a launch, parking area, or water-entry point, and must never be projected or auto-applied as one.

providers.name: North Dakota Game and Fish Department Lincoln Park boating access
providers.extractionMethod: The current North Dakota Game and Fish Department Fishing Facilities layer identifies ObjectID 1427 as an active, usable, 20-by-150-foot poured-concrete Red River boat ramp in the Lincoln Park/South Forks area, owned by the Grand Forks Park District. Its published GIS point lies on the upper portion of the visible ramp and is retained as the official facility anchor, not substituted for the water-entry coordinate.

providers.name: North Dakota Game and Fish Department and Minnesota DNR Lincoln Drive Park Landing
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR Red River State Water Trail Map 4 identifies Lincoln Drive Park Landing on the left/Grand Forks bank at river mile 304.1 as the trailer-access put-in for the official two-mile trip to LaFave Park. Visit Grand Forks independently directs users to the Lincoln Park boat ramp from Belmont Road and 13th Avenue South. The current North Dakota Game and Fish Department inventory identifies the matching active Grand Forks Park District poured-concrete ramp as ObjectID 1427 at 47.90888410499237, -97.02268528004571. Current Esri World Imagery shows that official point on the upper ramp; the coordinate below is the adjacent water-side end of the same visible concrete ramp, about 79 feet away. The distinct official facility anchor is preserved by provider ndgf_lincoln_drive_park_ramp_access_anchor.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Central Park N public water access inventory
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS02199 identifies Central Park N at river mile 13.8, administered by Anoka County, with a launch and one parking lot. The published GIS point is retained as the official facility/access anchor. The adjacent water-side slipway is represented separately by provider mn_dnr_rum_central_north_ramp_water_entry.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR and Anoka County Rum River Central Regional Park north ramp
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR Rum River Map 3 places the Central Regional Park trailer access, watercraft campsites, toilets, and drinking water at river mile 13.8. This uniquely selects the north facility: Minnesota public-water-access record WAS02199 is explicitly Central Park N at river mile 13.8, while the distinct Central Park S record WAS00323 is at river mile 10.7 near the map's fishing-pier/rest-area context. Anoka County's park page and summer map independently identify both a boat launch and canoe/kayak launch. The water-entry coordinate is the mapped slipway 8 feet from WAS02199; current Esri World Imagery aligns it with the north launch at the river edge.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Platte River State Park Decker Creek access
providers.extractionMethod: Nebraska Game and Parks identifies the canoe/kayak stop a few yards from the mouth of Decker Creek and publishes a photograph of the graded landing. Its Platte River Water Trail article gives the route topology: paddlers turn from the Platte up Decker Creek, pass under the railroad bridge, and reach the stop; the site was built as a river-accessible stop rather than a normal vehicle put-in/take-out, though boats may be wheeled down a maintenance road. The official photograph matches the uniquely shaped gravel landing, riprap, curved paved path, and footbridge visible in current Esri World Imagery. The coordinate is the water edge of that landing on the west bank of Decker Creek, immediately south of the footbridge.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission Loup River Water Trail Trip Planner
providers.extractionMethod: Decimal-degree start and end access-site coordinates transcribed from page 1 of the official Loup River Water Trail trip planner. The text identifies the Monroe Access Point as the public start, describes the downstream trip to Columbus, and publishes Start: 41.461082, -97.599121 / End: 41.418113, -97.367618. The coordinates are retained as access anchors rather than assumed water entries; the workflow derives water-entry coordinates independently from NHD hydrography. The accompanying page 2 map identifies water-access and parking symbols.

providers.name: National Park Service Tyler Bend upper launch parking area
providers.extractionMethod: The National Park Service identifies Tyler Bend as a primary boater access and describes the launch road connecting to its parking area. The NPS Tyler Bend area map places the boat launch on the upstream/west side of the bend. The facility coordinate is the center of the adjacent paved NPS parking footprint visible in current Esri World Imagery; it is retained separately from the water-entry coordinate.

providers.name: National Park Service Tyler Bend upper boat launch
providers.extractionMethod: The official NPS Tyler Bend area map marks the boat launch on the upstream/west side of the bend. The 2026 NPS concession operating plan removes the competing downstream feature from consideration by stating that only the Upper Tyler Bend access is available. The selected coordinate is the mapped upper gravel slipway, whose access road and shoreline landing align with current Esri World Imagery and the official map; the similarly named lower OSM slipway is not the currently authorized launch.

providers.name: City of Ann Arbor Gallup Park livery parking

The official parking coordinate is retained as the facility/access anchor and is intentionally separate from the Boat Dock water-entry feature.

providers.name: City of Ann Arbor Gallup Park livery Boat Dock

The official dock point agrees within about 15 feet with the center of two mapped livery piers and is used as the water entry; the separate east-side trailer slipway is not substituted for this livery route endpoint.

providers.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Rockhouse Access turnaround
providers.extractionMethod: AGFC states that its McIlroy Madison County WMA property joins the Kings River at Rockhouse Access, and The Nature Conservancy independently identifies Rockhouse as the AGFC-owned public access just upstream from the preserve. Kings River Arkansas describes a gravel road, ample parking, and a large gravel-bar launch near Rockhouse Creek. The facility anchor is the center of the unmistakable gravel turnaround connected to the independently mapped Rockhouse Boat Launch in current Esri World Imagery; it is stored separately from the shoreline water entry. This evidence class records official access identity plus transparent aerial derivation and is intentionally excluded from the unattended auto-apply source whitelist.

providers.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Rockhouse gravel-bar water entry
providers.extractionMethod: AGFC and The Nature Conservancy establish the named site's public identity and ownership. Natural Atlas independently maps Rockhouse Boat Launch at 36.28193372205891, -93.6639968409015 and classifies it as a gravel launch on Rockhouse Creek and the Kings River. At that exact point, current Esri World Imagery visibly shows the gravel access road and turnaround terminating at the west bank; a candidate-specific National Map query places it about 107 feet from the Kings River NHD centerline. The older local route-guide coordinate is rejected because it lands about 0.8 mile south in forest. This evidence class is retained for expert-reviewed corrections but is not whitelisted for unattended auto-apply.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Aqua Lane carry-in facility anchor

providers.name: Anoka County Rice Creek Water Trail Aqua Lane carry-in
providers.extractionMethod: The current Anoka County/RCWD Rice Creek Water Trail map places the Aqua Lane access immediately upstream of the road crossing, with limited parking east of the channel. Because its heads-up-digitized GIS point falls at the bridge/facility rather than a shoreline edge, the water entry below is derived separately at the east-bank water edge visible immediately upstream of the bridge in current Esri World Imagery. The DNR feature remains the distinct authoritative facility anchor.

providers.name: Ramsey County Long Lake Boat Landing parking anchor

The coordinate is the center of that unmistakable paved launch lot in current Esri World Imagery and is retained separately from the GPS-mapped concrete water entry.

providers.name: Maryland Antietam Creek Devil’s Backbone public canoe access

providers.name: New York Beaver River Canoe Route Moshier to High Falls access anchors

providers.name: New York Nine Mile Creek Munro Park to Pumphouse Road access anchors

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Long Lake Boat Landing water entry
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS01204 identifies the GPS-collected south-shore Long Lake facility, administered by Ramsey County, with two concrete-slab ramps, one dock, and trailer parking. The DNR GPS coordinate is therefore retained as the water entry rather than projected to the distant Rice Creek centerline.

providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC currently lists the Forked Lake Campground and Day Use Area hand launch, the Raquette River hand launch, and public North Point Road/Buttermilk Falls access in Sargent Ponds Wild Forest. providers.name: Carmans River Montauk Highway to Beaver Dam Road public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists the Carmans River hand launch off Montauk Highway with parking, a 300-yard carry, electric-motor restriction, and cooperative Wertheim Refuge access. The Town of Brookhaven documents a public kayak launch at the Beaver Dam Road end. The Beaver Dam coordinate is a generalized road-end waterline anchor and both sites require current field verification.

providers.name: Nissequogue River Paul T. Given to State Park public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists Paul T. Given County Park, Nissequogue River State Park, and Sunken Meadow State Park Field 3 as public kayak/canoe launch contexts with map coordinates. NYS Parks documents the tide window and mud-flat limitation at Nissequogue State Park; stored points require current confirmation of park hours, tide, water depth, carry, parking, and public landing.

providers.name: Peconic River River Road to Edwards Avenue public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists River Road East, River Road West, and the Mill Road at Edwards Avenue hand-launch contexts with map coordinates, carry/parking notes, and electric-motor restrictions. The Peconic River Blueway map independently identifies the upper launch sequence; stored points follow the state map anchors and remain subject to current permit, gate, carry, waterline, and dam-status confirmation.

providers.name: Peconic River Forge Pond to Upper Mills public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists the Forge Pond and Peconic River (Lower) Upper Mills launch contexts with map coordinates, launch types, parking/carry notes, and electric-motor restrictions. Suffolk County independently identifies the Route 25 Peconic River Canoe Launch as direct canoe/kayak access; stored points follow those official access anchors and require current ramp, carry, parking, waterline, and downstream-structure confirmation.

providers.name: Peconic River Upper Mills to Weeping Willow public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists the municipal Upper Mills and Weeping Willow hand-launch contexts plus the lower Peconic River unimproved trailer access with map coordinates, parking/carry notes, and electric-motor restrictions. Suffolk County independently confirms direct canoe/kayak access at the Route 25 Peconic River Canoe Launch, and the Peconic River Blueway map identifies the launch sequence. The route starts below the Upper Mills dam boundary and ends at Weeping Willow before the separate tidal/estuarine continuation.

providers.name: Peconic River Weeping Willow to Indian Island public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: The Peconic Estuary Partnership identifies Weeping Willow and Indian Island as sequential launch sites on the Peconic River Blueway. NYSDEC independently publishes the Weeping Willow and lower-river access coordinates, while Suffolk County confirms Indian Island self-launch boating at the estuarine mouth. The Indian Island point follows an official estuary-plan shoreline-area coordinate rather than a surveyed dock coordinate; confirm the exact landing, tide, beach, and park conditions before use.

providers.name: Houston District I Fonde Park / Lidstone Street canoe-kayak launch
providers.extractionMethod: Houston District I identifies the built Brays Bayou canoe/kayak launch near Fonde Park at 2600 Lidstone Street. The address resolves to the north end of the Lidstone bridge; current Esri World Imagery shows the launch path descending from the Brays Bayou Greenway to the north bank immediately west of that bridge. The stored point uses that visible water-entry end rather than the interior Fonde Park map pin.

providers.name: Iowa DNR Winnebago River Fertile Mill Park public-access anchor
providers.extractionMethod: Iowa DNR's statewide public-water-access inventory identifies Fertile Mill Park as a city-owned Winnebago River access with a natural launch surface, gravel parking, and a 13-foot parking-to-access distance. The route's William Rhodes Island Park below-dam coordinate is retained as the below-dam arrival/launch-area anchor because the city and county route materials identify the Fertile dam complex, while the DNR feature is offset from the generalized NHD flowline and does not establish the exact wetted-edge launch. Confirm the safe below-dam carry and avoid dam hydraulics before launch.

providers.name: Iowa DNR Mahaska County South Skunk River public water accesses
providers.extractionMethod: Iowa DNR's statewide public-water-access inventory identifies the Mahaska County Conservation Board Glendale and Rose Hill concrete ramps on the South Skunk River. The stored points are the inventory's water-access geometries, not the erroneous broad Google Maps area anchors previously embedded by the county park pages.

providers.name: Indiana County Parks Waterworks Conservation Area canoe/kayak launch
providers.extractionMethod: Indiana County Parks' site map marks a canoe/kayak launch on the park-side bank of Two Lick Creek. The county directions page supplies the current park pin; the launch point is placed on the corresponding county-map bank position and checked against the USGS NHD Two Lick Creek flowline. This replaces a third-party geotrail coordinate that resolved to a house several miles west of the park.

providers.name: National Park Service / Fort Niobrara NWR Launch Site
providers.extractionMethod: Recreation.gov publishes the Fort Niobrara Wilderness access GPS coordinate for the refuge canoe launch; the NPS identifies the same site as the public canoe/kayak launch adjacent to Cornell Bridge.

providers.name: Cumberland County Conodoguinet Creek Water Trail access table
providers.extractionMethod: The current Cumberland County access table identifies B5, Vincent DiFilippo Nature Preserve, as a named concrete Conodoguinet launch and publishes 40.2561, -77.0192. The official table coordinate is retained as the shared launch pin; it is not projected to an NHD centerline.

providers.name: NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail Sidney to Bainbridge itinerary map pins
providers.extractionMethod: Named itinerary map pins from the NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail. Coordinates are public access-area anchors for the water-entry points, not a claim that the parking centroid is the exact wetted-edge pixel.

providers.name: NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail Southern Tier itinerary map pins
providers.extractionMethod: Named itinerary map pins from the NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail. Coordinates are public access-area anchors for the water-entry points, not a claim that the parking centroid is the exact wetted-edge pixel.

providers.name: NYSDEC Chenango River Greene and Chenango Forks launch listings
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC county launch tables publish the Greene Chenango River hand launch and the Chenango Forks Route 12 hand launch coordinates. The Chenango Forks coordinate is on the Tioughnioga immediately upstream of its junction with the Chenango; that connected-water endpoint relationship is preserved rather than silently treating the two named waterbodies as identical.

providers.name: NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail Chemung itinerary map pins
providers.extractionMethod: Named itinerary map pins from the NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail. Coordinates are public access-area anchors for water-entry points, not a claim that the parking centroid is the exact wetted-edge pixel. The Wyncoop Creek Road point is retained only as an itinerary-described unofficial rest stop and is not used as an authoritative public access control.

providers.name: Unadilla River Rockdale to Sidney public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: Otsego Outdoors identifies the Rockdale-to-Sidney paddle as a public, slow-moving route maintained by NYSDEC and names the Batterson Road put-in and Sidney DEC/confluence take-out. CanWePaddle supplies the route map links and confirms the named endpoint areas; coordinates are retained as public water-entry anchors rather than parking centroids.

providers.name: West Branch Delaware River Hale Eddy to Balls Eddy public access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Hale Eddy hand launch coordinate. Upper Delaware public-access sources identify Balls Eddy as the public Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission take-out; the cross-border endpoint is preserved with its own access source and rule-check caveat.

providers.name: Allegheny County North Park Lake boat-launch area
providers.extractionMethod: Allegheny County identifies the 66-acre North Park Lake and boathouse as a kayaking/boating facility; its current Boathouse Lawn event page publishes 40.60499534620007, -80.00685229073453 for the named boating area. The county's North Park history explains that North Park Lake is fed by North Fork Pine Creek and empties into Pine Creek, documenting the connected-water relationship for this Little Pine Creek route start.

providers.name: Tioughnioga River Cortland to Marathon public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Cortland County Tioughnioga launch coordinates and Cortland County identifies the Yaman Park hand launch and Marathon launch, including parking, carry, and water-entry descriptions. Yaman Park is listed on the East Branch access system, so that connected-water relationship is retained rather than hidden.

providers.name: Schoharie Creek Esperance to Burtonsville public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Esperance hand-launch coordinate and 500-foot carry in Schoharie County, and the Montgomery County launch listing publishes the Burtonsville hand-launch coordinate. The endpoint pair is retained as public water-entry anchors with limited parking and carry caveats.

providers.name: Genesee River Avon to Scottsville public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Avon hand launch in Livingston County and the Wheatland/Scottsville-area hand launch in Monroe County, including coordinates and parking. The Blueway route map provides independent public-access and hazard context for the same main-stem corridor.

providers.name: Wallkill River Popp Park to Gardiner public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: The Wallkill River Watershed Alliance inventory identifies Popp Park at 3081 Route 208 and Gardiner Launch at 215 Farmer's Turnpike as active launches, and the Orange County map names Section 07 Popp Park to Gardiner Launch. Stored coordinates are generalized access-area anchors and require current field verification.

providers.name: Wallkill River Gardiner to New Paltz public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: The Wallkill River Watershed Alliance inventory identifies an active Gardiner launch at 215 Farmer's Turnpike, while NYSDEC publishes the New Paltz hand-launch coordinate. The Gardiner map and route-source pin are generalized, so the access-area uncertainty and verification caveat remain explicit.

providers.name: Wallkill River New Paltz to Rosendale public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists current public Wallkill River hand launches at New Paltz and Rosendale, while the Wallkill River Watershed Alliance access inventory distinguishes the same sites as active launches. Stored coordinates are launch-area anchors and require current carry, parking, dock, and posted-rule verification.

providers.name: Batten Kill Eagleville to Battenville public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC identifies the Batten Kill State Forest Eagleville Road parking area and hand launch with a current coordinate. The route-specific field report identifies CR 61 in Battenville as the take-out, matching the existing downstream Battenville route; both coordinates are waterline/access-area anchors and require field verification.

providers.name: Batten Kill Battenville to Clarks Mills public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: CanWePaddle identifies the Battenville NY Route 61 access and the Clarks Mills/Rexleigh take-out area. NYSDEC’s Batten Kill public-fishing-rights map supplies the public-access corridor and private-bank context; the endpoint pins are access-area anchors rather than surveyed ramp coordinates and must be verified on site.

providers.name: Cattaraugus Creek Gowanda to Sunset Bay public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: New York planning documents identify Zoar Valley Gateway Park in Gowanda as a public waterfront park with a watercraft launch. NYS Parks and Chautauqua County identify the public Cattaraugus Creek launch at Sunset Bay off Ann Street/Allegany Road. The intervening creek corridor includes the Seneca Nation Cattaraugus Territory, so endpoint listings do not by themselves authorize travel; confirm current Nation permission or restrictions before launch.

providers.name: Cattaraugus Creek Zoar Bridge to Gowanda public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC currently identifies the North Otto Road Cattaraugus Creek Waterway Access as a public hand launch with a 250-foot carry and describes the Gowanda take-out immediately downstream of the Aldrich Street bridge. American Whitewater publishes the matching Zoar Bridge-to-Gowanda endpoint anchors and direct Gowanda gauge relationship; NYSDOT and Gowanda planning documents corroborate the Aldrich Street/Gowanda public waterfront access context. Coordinates remain access-area anchors and require current field confirmation of the landing, parking, and posted rules.

providers.name: Oswegatchie River Inlet to High Falls public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Inlet Road hand-launch coordinate on the Oswegatchie River and identifies the remote Oswegatchie canoe route, High Falls obstruction, river campsites, and High Falls lean-tos. The High Falls coordinate is retained as a water-side turnaround/portage boundary rather than a vehicle take-out; do not infer a runnable passage over the falls.

providers.name: Oswegatchie River Heuvelton to Ogdensburg public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC currently lists the municipal Heuvelton Oswegatchie launch and the Eel Weir State Park Oswegatchie launch with public water-entry coordinates and parking capacities. The St. Lawrence Valley Paddlers’ current Remington I course identifies the same downstream corridor and the Eel Weir dam portage; stored points remain access-area anchors requiring current launch, carry, and park-rule confirmation.

providers.name: Oswegatchie River Heuvelton to Ogdensburg finish access anchor
providers.extractionMethod: The current St. Lawrence Valley Paddlers Remington I course identifies a boat-launch finish under the Lafayette Spring Street bridge in Ogdensburg. The state water-quality record identifies the Oswegatchie waterline at that bridge; this is retained as a community-documented finish/access anchor rather than an assumed municipal ramp, and must be confirmed with Ogdensburg before ordinary-day use.

providers.name: Raquette River Raymondville to Massena Springs public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: The current NYSDEC Raquette River page specifically directs canoeists to put in off River Road 0.6 mile downstream of Raymondville Dam and identifies Massena Springs Town Park as the take-out with a boat launch. The stored points are water-adjacent access-area anchors requiring current confirmation of the exact carry, parking, water entry, landing, hours, and posted power or municipal boundaries; they do not convert the nearby USGS gauge property or every park bank into launch permission.

providers.name: New York St. Lawrence River Louisville to Massena public launch controls
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC's current St. Lawrence County launch directory identifies the Wilson Hill Wildlife Management Area launch in Louisville on the St. Lawrence River and the Massena launch on the St. Lawrence River, with published public-launch coordinates and parking capacities. Retain the agency coordinates as the access controls; the coordinate audit separately records that NHD's generalized named flowline is distant from these broad, power-managed river and waterbody launch areas. Confirm the exact carry, waterline, vessel traffic, posted power notices, and landing before staging.

providers.name: New York lower Niagara River Lewiston to Fort Niagara public launch controls
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC's current Niagara County launch directory identifies public hard-surface lower Niagara River launch contexts at Lewiston Landing, the Youngstown/Porter municipal site, and Fort Niagara State Park, with published water-specific coordinates and parking context. Retain those agency coordinates as authoritative access-area controls, while preserving the route's same-day checks for ramp assignment, limited parking, current, vessel traffic, park or municipal rules, Lake Ontario mouth conditions, and the hard Fort Niagara finish.

providers.name: New York Middle Branch St. Regis Route 458 to St. Regis Falls access controls
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC's current Franklin County launch directory lists the Santa Clara Flow/St. Regis River public hard-surface launch at 44.630675,-74.453463 with parking for approximately ten cars and trailers. The Town of Waverly owns and operates the St. Regis Falls Scenic Campsite at the downstream finish; that finish is permission-based, so preserve current check-in, landing, parking, and camping authorization rather than treating the campground as an unconditional public ramp.

providers.name: New York West Branch St. Regis Five Mile hand-launch access controls
providers.extractionMethod: The current NYSDEC Raquette Boreal Complex page names four Five Mile hand-launch parking areas, publishes coordinates for each, documents a 0.4-mile carry at Hand Launch Parking Area #3, and authorizes seasonal paddling on the designated West Branch St. Regis River section. Retain the four points as access-area controls, preserve the May 1–September 30 public-use window, and require current road, gate, carry, waterline, logging, camp-lease, and signed-portage confirmation before launch.

providers.name: East Canada Creek Powley Place short out-and-back public access
providers.extractionMethod: The current NYSDEC Ferris Lake Wild Forest page publishes the Powley Place Hand Launch coordinate and specifically describes paddling almost two miles downstream to the head of the rapids, with an island turn-around and beaver-dam limit upstream. The route uses the DEC-supported short outing as an out-and-back and retains the island point only as a water objective and hard turn-around landmark, not a public take-out.

providers.name: Sacandaga River Speculator to Duck Bay flatwater loop public access
providers.extractionMethod: The current NYSDEC Perkins Clearing and Speculator Tree Farm page publishes the Speculator Ball Field hand launch and Duck Bay Picnic Area hand launch, describes the almost-five-mile flatwater round trip, and distinguishes the route from the hydropower dam and downstream rapids/cascades. Both stored points are water-adjacent access-area anchors requiring current confirmation of parking, carry, landing, and local restrictions.

providers.name: Kunjamuk River Speculator to Elm Lake out-and-back public access
providers.extractionMethod: The current NYSDEC page identifies the Speculator Ball Field hand launch and the Kunjamuk branch, and describes the village-launch-to-Elm-Lake outing as an approximately 12-mile round trip with beaver-dam/obstacle conditions. The current DEC recreation-management material says the proposed Elm Lake car-top launch is no longer accessible, so the Speculator point is the only claimed vehicle/water endpoint and the Elm Lake point is retained only as a water objective/turn-around anchor.

providers.name: Marion River Blue Mountain Lake to Raquette Lake public access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC identifies the five-mile Marion River Scenic reach in the Sargent Ponds Wild Forest. Current regional paddling guidance identifies Blue Mountain Lake Town Beach as the lake's only public boat launch, and the Raquette Lake management plan plus current regional launch listing identify the Village General Store launch as public. Both coordinates are retained as access-area anchors requiring current waterline, parking, carry, inspection, and operating-status confirmation; the Bassett Carry is a mandatory portage around the Utowana dam/rapids.

providers.name: Dead Creek Route 3 headwaters out-and-back public access
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC Raquette Boreal Complex guidance identifies Dead Creek as a distinct three-mile paddling route. The DEC unit-management plan identifies the Route 3 pull-off/DOT parking and informal put-in, while the current regional paddling guide supplies the route-specific pull-off, picnic-area, 20-yard carry, and access-area coordinate. This is an access-area anchor, not a formal launch facility; confirm the roadside pull-off, path, waterline, and parking on site.

providers.name: Osgood Pond and Osgood River out-and-back public access
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC Paul Smiths College Conservation Easement guidance lists the Osgood Pond Hand Launch Site at 44.44319, -74.23838 and states that the launch provides access to Osgood Pond and the Osgood River. The route-specific regional guide corroborates the pond-to-river paddle and river conditions. The control is the DEC-listed vehicle access anchor; the Meacham Lake mouth objective remains water-only.

providers.name: North Branch Saranac River North Branch Road out-and-back public access
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC Kushaqua Conservation Easement guidance identifies the North Branch Road Parking Area and describes a 460-foot walk plus a 115-foot path to a docked hand launch on the North Branch Saranac River at approximately 44.5114, -74.1472. The launch is restricted to non-motorized watercraft. The stored coordinate is the public water-entry anchor; the Lake Kushaqua approach remains a water-only turnaround objective.

providers.name: Grass River DeGrasse to Pyrites public access
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC guidance identifies the DeGrasse State Forest hand launch on the South Branch Grass River at 44.3681946, -75.07724. A current NYS DPS access document identifies the public, ADA-accessible kayak/canoe launch just north of Pyrites on the Grasse River with Route 21 access and safe roadside loading/unloading. These controls bound the planning-only DeGrasse-to-Pyrites corridor; the Pyrites hydropower dam and any downstream portage remain outside the route.

providers.name: Boquet River Route 73 to Split Rock public access
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC Giant Mountain Wilderness guidance identifies the Boquet River Parking Area on Route 73 at 44.1051, -73.6920, and the current North Fork Boquet biological survey describes easy public access along Route 73. Current NYSDEC Hammond Pond Wild Forest guidance identifies a primitive tent site on the Boquet River bank a short distance upstream of Split Rock Falls and states primitive sites are usually accessible by hiking or paddling. These controls bound the route conservatively above Split Rock Falls; both coordinates remain access-area/campsite anchors requiring field verification of the exact waterline and carry.

providers.name: Little River Youngs Road to Streeter Lake Road public hand launches
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC Aldrich Pond Wild Forest guidance identifies the nearly 7-mile Little River paddling corridor, both named hand launches and the short carry around Schuler Fall. The current Adirondack backcountry notice also records a temporary closure at the Youngs Road launch for a culvert-related road reroute, so these controls establish the documented public access locations but do not override a posted closure or replace field confirmation of the waterline, parking, carry, and seasonal road status.

providers.name: Emmons to West Oneonta Susquehanna public hand launches
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYS Parks/NYSDEC launch listings identify the Emmons and West Oneonta Susquehanna River hand launches. These controls establish public water-entry locations for the bounded gap section but still require field verification of carry, parking, waterline, traffic, and current posted rules.

providers.name: West Oneonta to Otego Susquehanna public hand launches
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC Otsego County launch listings identify the Oneonta and Otego Susquehanna River hand launches and publish their access-area coordinates. Otsego Outdoors independently publishes the matching nine-mile West Oneonta-to-Otego/Wells Bridge moving-flatwater itinerary. These controls establish public water-entry locations but still require field verification of the carry, parking, waterline, bridge traffic, and current posted rules.

providers.name: Otego to Unadilla Susquehanna public hand launches
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYS Parks/NYSDEC launch listings identify the Otego/Wells Bridge and Unadilla Susquehanna River hand launches. These controls establish public water-entry locations for the bounded gap section but still require field verification of carry, parking, waterline, traffic, and current posted rules.

providers.name: Unadilla to Sidney Susquehanna public hand launches
providers.extractionMethod: Current NYSDEC launch listings identify the Unadilla and Sidney Susquehanna River hand launches and publish their access-area coordinates. CanWePaddle publishes the parent Unadilla-to-Bainbridge Class I corridor and direct Unadilla gauge context; the route intentionally ends at Sidney, the existing downstream PaddleToday boundary, to avoid duplicating the Sidney-to-Bainbridge reach. Both controls remain access-area anchors requiring same-day verification of the carry, parking, waterline, landing, and posted rules.

providers.name: Raquette River Axton Landing to The Crusher public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Axton Landing hand-launch coordinate on Coreys Road and the Raquette River Crusher launch coordinate in the Saranac Lakes Wild Forest. The route’s regional paddling sources identify the matching nine-mile Axton-to-Crusher corridor; the route remains planning-only because its live same-river gauge is downstream and no numeric threshold is published.

providers.name: NYSDEC Raquette River Dead Creek to Jamestown Falls public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC identifies the Dead Creek Route 3 pull-off/picnic-area access and path to an informal put-in, the Moody Falls hand launch with a 0.1-mile carry, and the Jamestown Falls hand launch with a 100-foot carry. The Dead Creek coordinate is retained as a larger-uncertainty access-area anchor because DEC describes the entry but does not publish a surveyed waterline coordinate; all points require current field verification, and no private-bank substitute is implied.

providers.name: Susquehanna River Cooperstown to Phoenix Mills public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: The NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail itinerary and map identify Fish Road Launch on Otsego Lake and Compton Bridge NYS DEC Fishing Access as the public endpoints of the bounded 5.5-mile Cooperstown-to-Phoenix-Mills route. The route includes a mandatory Otsego Lake Dam portage and a lake-to-river transition; coordinates are retained as public water-entry anchors, not town-center geocodes.

providers.name: Susquehanna River Crumhorn Pond to Goodyear Lake public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: The NY Susquehanna Basin Water Trail itinerary and map identify Crumhorn Pond / Susquehanna State Forest, Portlandville, and Goodyear Lake / Silliman Cove as public water-entry points for the bounded 3.25–6-mile route. The corridor includes a slow-current river-to-lake transition and a hard Colliers Dam boundary; coordinates are retained as public water-entry anchors, not residential or town-center geocodes.

providers.name: Mohawk River Herkimer to Little Falls public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: CanWePaddle identifies the eight-mile Herkimer-to-Little-Falls Erie Canalway reach and its endpoint areas; NYSDEC lists the selected Herkimer and Rotary Park public launches and coordinates. The route is canalized and ends at the Lock 17/Rotary Park boundary; coordinates are public water-entry anchors.

providers.name: East Branch Ausable River Hulls Falls to Keene public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: Lake Placid publishes the bounded 6.3-mile East Branch Ausable Hulls Falls-to-Keene reach, exact endpoint coordinates, and Class II–V+ water-level-dependent character. American Whitewater indexes the distinct reach as IV(V). Coordinates are retained as route-source public water-entry anchors requiring current field verification, including confirmation that the Hulls Falls pin is below the falls and legally usable.

providers.name: East Branch Ausable River Keene to Upper Jay public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: Lake Placid publishes the bounded 6.3-mile East Branch Ausable Keene-to-Upper-Jay reach, exact endpoint coordinates, and Class II–III water-level-dependent character. The Adirondack Park Agency guide supplies the broader East Branch paddling and bridge-entry context. Coordinates are retained as route-source public water-entry anchors requiring current field verification.

providers.name: West Branch Ausable River Wilmington to Au Sable Forks public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: Lake Placid publishes the bounded 11-mile West Branch Ausable Wilmington-to-Au-Sable-Forks reach, exact endpoint coordinates, and Class I–III+ whitewater designation. The APA Wilmington visitor guide identifies Route 86/River Road water-entry context, while NYSDEC warns that much of the branch is inaccessible, rocky, shallow, or unsuitable for general paddling. Coordinates are retained as route-source public water-entry anchors requiring current field verification.

providers.name: East Kill Beaches Corners to Jewett Center public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: American Whitewater publishes the named 5.4-mile East Kill Class II–IV reach, its direct USGS 01349700 correlation, 300–1,200 cfs planning band, Mill Hollow feature, and bridge-based endpoint sequence. Riverfacts publishes route-specific coordinate anchors for the Beaches Corners put-in and Route 23A take-out. NYSDEC public-fishing-rights mapping and NYSDOT bridge records corroborate the East Kill stream and bridge corridor. Both stored points are water-adjacent access-area anchors requiring current confirmation of legal parking, carry, and landing.

providers.name: East Canada Creek Dolgeville to Route 5 public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: Montgomery County publishes the distinct approximately 8-mile Dolgeville-to-Route 5 route, endpoint coordinates, and mildly difficult description. Riverfacts independently publishes the same route-map coordinate pair, and the Brookfield East Canada Creek access-study filing records the reach as Class I–III. NYSDEC PFR mapping supplies stream/parking context but is treated as fishing-rights information rather than blanket boating authorization. Both stored points are water-adjacent access-area anchors requiring current confirmation of legal parking, carry, and landing.

providers.name: West Canada Creek Middleville to Kast Bridge public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: American Whitewater publishes the Middleville-to-Kast Bridge Class II–II+ section, while the West Canada Creek access study identifies NYSDEC Rec Site 9 north of Middleville and the Kast Bridge access area. USGS flood documentation fixes the Route 28 Bridge Street crossing coordinate at Middleville and USGS station data fixes the Kast Bridge vicinity. Both stored points are access-area anchors requiring current field confirmation, not guaranteed maintained ramps.

providers.name: Middle Branch St. Regis River Silver Staircase public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: American Whitewater publishes the named 11.1-mile Silver Staircase reach and Riverfacts publishes the endpoint coordinate pair. The Town of Waverly documents the riverfront campground at St. Regis Falls. Nicholville and Fort Jackson remain conditional access-area anchors requiring current field confirmation.

providers.name: South Sandy Creek Route 95 to Route 11 public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: American Whitewater publishes the named 11.6-mile Route 95-to-Route 11 Lorraine Gulf reach and identifies the route-specific access corridor. NYSDEC publishes public fishing-rights mapping for the Route 95/Bullock Corners area and a current Lakeview Wildlife Management Area cartop launch on South Sandy Creek. The upper point is retained as a conditional access-area anchor pending field confirmation; the lower point is the DEC launch anchor.

providers.name: Schroon River Starbuckville to Riverbank public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC lists the public Starbuckville Dam hand launch, and regional paddling guidance identifies the Warren County Canoe and Kayak Access on East Schroon River Road as the Riverbank take-out. American Whitewater identifies the same 6.7-mile reach and a Route 8 alternate put-in. The Riverbank and alternate points are access-area anchors requiring current field verification, especially around private shoreline.

providers.name: Schroon River Schroon Falls to Schroon Lake public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: NYSDEC publishes the Schroon Falls Hand Launch just below the falls and the municipal Schroon Lake Dock Street launch; current regional guidance describes the upper Schroon river-to-lake paddle. Both controls are current public launch anchors, while the route distance and final river-to-lake landing remain subject to field verification.

providers.name: Schroon River South Horicon Bridge to Starbuckville public paddling access
providers.extractionMethod: Current launch listings identify the municipal South Horicon Bridge hand launch and the Starbuckville Dam hand launch. Town and regional planning material describes the intervening Schroon River as a canoe/kayak corridor with Class II water and bridge/choke-point concerns.
